dimensions.assessment: Affects entities applying for high-cost universal service program funding to deploy broadband networks in rural and high-cost areas.
dimensions.evidence: applicants for, and other recipients of, a new covered funding award

dimensions.assessment: Establishes rigorous technical, financial, and operational vetting standards and mandatory financial penalties for pre-authorization defaults.
dimensions.evidence: set a penalty for pre-authorization defaults of at least $9,000 per violation and may not limit the base forfeiture to an amount less than 30 percent of the applicant's total support

dimensions.assessment: Affects the distribution mechanisms and potential forfeiture collections associated with federal high-cost universal service fund grants.
dimensions.evidence: any new offer of high-cost universal service program funding ... for the deployment of a broadband-capable network

dimensions.assessment: Amends section 254 of the Communications Act of 1934 to mandate a new FCC rulemaking proceeding and compliance standard framework.
dimensions.evidence: the Commission shall initiate a rulemaking proceeding to establish a vetting process for applicants

dimensions.assessment: Creates permanent vetting rules and penalty structures for all new funding awards issued after the rulemaking concludes.
dimensions.evidence: award of covered funding that is made based on an application submitted to the Commission on or after the date on which rules are promulgated

missing_information: Total aggregate dollar amounts of high-cost universal service program funds impacted by the vetting rules.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the FCC to establish a rulemaking process to vet prospective high-cost universal service program funding applicants for broadband deployment, mandating technical qualifications and pre-authorization penalties.
